fields.reasoning: The change set's intent asks exactly for this: a run the daemon drives takes rhiza.daemon.permissionMode when the start names none, so an owner or orchestrator can queue plan runs without choosing a mode (the 2026-11-13 acceptEdits run stalled on a permission prompt). Checking with the daemon's setting at queue time keeps the existing guarantee in run.go that a start whose agent steps cannot run is refused before any git or write, while recording no mode lets daemonStartsQueued apply the setting current at start time rather than freezing a copy. A foreground start or an unset daemon setting has no mode to fall back on, so the agent step genuinely cannot run; keeping the refusal there is the safe, minimal choice, and naming the setting in the message points users at the new way out. Both halves are the question-asker's own recommendations and fit the code (checkAgentSteps at run.go:672/695, daemon.go:128 already checks with conf.mode).
fields.statement: A run start that names no --permission-mode and is queued for the daemon (not --foreground) is checked at queue time with rhiza.daemon.permissionMode standing in for the mode (checkAgentSteps gets the daemon's setting), and is queued with no mode recorded, so the daemon fills in its own rhiza.daemon.permissionMode when it starts the run, as it already does for its own picks. When the start names no mode and rhiza.daemon.permissionMode is unset, or the start is --foreground (no daemon drives it), today's refusal stays, and its message names rhiza.daemon.permissionMode as a third way out next to --permission-mode and the step's permission_mode. Anything that re-checks a queued run's agent steps before the daemon starts it uses the same stand-in.
